newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Three firms apply for S.Korea satellite deal - paper.
newsitem.headline: Three firms apply for S.Korea satellite deal - paper.

text.p: Two U.S. firms and a French company have applied for an estimated 80 billion won contract to build a communications satellite for South Korea, a local newspaper reported on Sunday.

The Korea Times, quoting state Korea Telecom Corp officials, said Lockheed Martin Corp and Hughes Space and Communications International Inc, both from the United States, and Aerospatiale of France had applied for the contract.
Korea Telecom will conclude a contract with one successful applicant on January 30 next year, the newspaper said.
The satellite will be built between March 1997 and June 1999 and put into service in September 1999, it added.
Korea Telecom officials could not be reached for comment.
